added_failures_note: measured by the reviewing run through the production path: annotate_review_of_run over the reviewed run's own manifest names baseline_suite=base_suite.log and after_suite=after_suite.log, and added_failures_from_gate_logs reads both texts (22 passed at c3d1db19, 22 passed at 68723fdb) and returns (0, []) — a set difference over pytest node ids, so the zero is a measurement, not an absence. The three behaviours this review was fenced to answer are recorded under evidence_checks with the command and output that answered each.

evidence_checks.check: a checkpoint whose recorded st_dev differs while the inode matches continues
a replaced stream still falls back
an arm with no continuable checkpoint emits zero transition rows and zero rows for another session
evidence_checks.command: same probe, section (3); cross-checked end to end by probe_continue_end_to_end.py

findings.text: the two all() assertions (lines 193 and 196) hold vacuously over an empty emitted list and nothing in the test asserts the baseline row the done-when names, so a regression that stops the first arm emitting anything — or that silently drops the derived fleet — leaves this test green; my probe shows the healthy arm emits exactly one baseline row (probe_host_change.log, "baseline rows for this session: 1"), so one presence assertion would close the gap.

the artifacts line states "1 failed / 2 passed at base c3d1db19" as the headline metric, but the run directory holds no single-invocation log of the whole test file at base — control-dev-and-ino.log records only the one host-change test ("1 failed in 0.49s") — so the two-passed half of the figure is unverifiable from the run's own evidence (I reproduced the figure independently in base-arm-new-tests.log, "1 failed, 2 passed in 1.09s", but that log is not the run's).

item_verdicts.diff: four commits span c3d1db19..dd121d36: 0867a75e fix(crew): continue a follower across a host change on a shared mount drops the recorded dev from continues()'s comparison (the line becomes an inode-only test) and rewrites the stream_identity and continues docstrings to say the device is carried beside the inode but not part of the answer; 68723fdb tidies the new test file; e0bc5bd5 and dd121d36 touch docs only (3 changed lines across the evidence and plan HTML), and none of the four commits changes a plan-* meta line.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when is three quantitative claims — a checkpoint whose recorded st_dev differs while the inode matches continues, a replaced stream still falls back, and an arm with no continuable checkpoint emits zero transition rows and zero rows for another session — the gate in tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py:98,128,154 asserts all three and gate.log records "3 passed" at code head 68723fdb, while my own base arm at c3d1db19 (base-arm-new-tests.log) records "1 failed, 2 passed in 1.09s" with the host-change test failing at line 123 on "assert False is True", and my head-arm re-run (head-arm-new-tests.log) records "3 passed in 1.29s"; the third claim is asserted only as two all() over the emitted rows (:193, :196), which an empty emission would also satisfy.
item_verdicts.goal: the reviewed goal is that a follower re-armed after a host change on the shared filesystem continues from its checkpoint instead of replaying the whole stream, and reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py:120 continues() now decides the stream identity on the inode alone, which my probe at head dd121d36 (probe_host_change.log, scratch RECKON_HOME under /tmp) measures directly: a checkpoint recorded with identity {'dev': 64774, 'ino': 100985872} against a stream that now stats as {'dev': 64772, 'ino': 100985872} prints "continues(record, stream) -> True", and the end-to-end probe (probe_continue_end_to_end.log) shows the same divergence making _follow_resume_plan choose "continue" at head where the base-arm source chooses "restart".
item_verdicts.manifest: the manifest names four gate logs with their counts (gate.log "3 passed", control-dev-and-ino.log "1 failed", base_suite.log and after_suite.log "22 passed" each), states the head gate with its command and revision, and names its negative control log whose first line repeats the declared string verbatim; the one figure it carries that no log on disk spans is manifest.md:24, the full-file base arm "1 failed / 2 passed at base c3d1db19", whose recorded provenance control-dev-and-ino.log covers only the single red test (tail: "1 failed in 0.49s") — I reproduced the full-file figure myself, so it is true, but a reader of the run's own evidence cannot check it.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared fence is seven paths (reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py, reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/runs.py, tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py, the landing-record HTML, docs/figures/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet, the plan HTML) and git diff --name-only c3d1db19 dd121d36 lists exactly five files — reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py, tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py, and the three docs paths — all inside the fence and set-equal to the manifest's changed_paths, with reckon/cli.py and reckon/crew/runs.py untouched as the node's evidence_inputs says was not needed.

justifications.durability: the foreign-device test (tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py:98) fails on the unmodified base source at line 123, which is precisely the regression it guards, and the replaced-stream test (:128) names its failing condition; but the arm test's two all() assertions (:193, :196) also pass over an empty emitted list and nothing asserts the baseline row the done-when names, so a regression that emits nothing at all leaves this file green.
justifications.evidence: the three claims are asserted by tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py:98,128,154 and every recorded result is reproduced by arms I ran myself at both revisions (base-arm-new-tests.log "1 failed, 2 passed"; head-arm-new-tests.log "3 passed"), with the declared negative-control string verbatim on line 1 of control-dev-and-ino.log; the withheld points are the base-arm full-file figure having no covering log in the run directory and the zero-transition claim resting on assertions an empty emission satisfies.
justifications.fit: the change keeps the module's idiom — a plain identity comparison plus a docstring stating why the device is carried and not compared (reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py:104-124) — reuses the file's existing test helpers, and a check of the five changed paths against the repository naming rules found no banned label or identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py:120-124 is exactly the inode-only comparison the goal requires and probe_continue_end_to_end.log shows _follow_resume_plan choosing "continue" at head where the same probe over the base source chooses "restart"; one point is withheld because "instead of replaying the whole stream" is verified at fixture scale only — the incident's days-of-history replay cannot be reproduced inside this review's budget.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only c3d1db19 dd121d36 is set-equal to the manifest's five changed_paths, each inside the seven-path fence, and the diff carries nothing beyond the inode-only comparison plus its tests and its plan and evidence records.
